criticReviews.author: Austin Fimmano
criticReviews.excerpt: "The show has its high points. A dance number lit by phone flashlights has a uniquely 2020s feel, and the choreography tells a clear story about how our relationship to our phones can keep us from focusing on real life."

criticReviews.author: Hayley Levitt
criticReviews.excerpt: "It’s wholesome charm and energizing dance sitting on a bed of new-year-new-me platitudes best served on a For You Page. That’s the thing about quick bites. They’re tasty, but they don’t fill you up."

criticReviews.author: Austin Fimmano
criticReviews.excerpt: "The show has its high points. A dance number lit by phone flashlights has a uniquely 2020s feel, and the choreography tells a clear story about how our relationship to our phones can keep us from focusing on real life."

criticReviews.author: Ryan Leeds
criticReviews.excerpt: "in a cultural moment defined by isolation, cynicism, and endless scroll, 11 to Midnight offers something genuinely subversive: communal joy."

criticReviews.author: Julia Rank
criticReviews.excerpt: "Anne Boleyn's fate is a strong catalyst for this colourfully anachronistic exploration of sexual politics"

criticReviews.author: Nick Curtis
criticReviews.excerpt: “It’s a bold, idiosyncratic and disturbingly funny work that slightly overplays its hand towards the end.”

criticReviews.author: Andrzej Lukowski
criticReviews.excerpt: “1536 is a droll and perceptive period piece that’s also a searing and unsettling contemporary feminist drama.”

criticReviews.author: Clive Davis
criticReviews.excerpt: “What you actually get is the kind of simplistic, feminist-lite drama about the evils of patriarchy that you normally encounter in a one-hour slot at the Edinburgh Fringe.”

criticReviews.author: Sarah Crompton
criticReviews.excerpt: “This is an original and exciting debut, given an exceptional production by director Lyndsey Turner and an outstanding cast.”

criticReviews.author: Sam Marlowe
criticReviews.excerpt: “The play’s greatest tragedy is the warping of their relationship by the patriarchal hierarchy in which they are forced to exist.”

criticReviews.author: Claire Allfree
criticReviews.excerpt: "extremely funny debut refreshes the tired story of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn by filtering it through the perspective of three market village girls who look like Tudor peasants but speak like potty-mouthed Gen Zedders.”

criticReviews.author: Rachel Halliburton
criticReviews.excerpt: “1536 is a foul-mouthed, furious, frenetically funny ride through the lives of three young women living in Henry VIII’s England.”

criticReviews.author: Miriam Gillinson
criticReviews.excerpt: "1536 is an effortlessly funny, bold and ballsy play"

criticReviews.author: Ella Duggan
criticReviews.excerpt: “1536 is a love letter to female friendship and a sharp dissection of how systemic misogyny deforms even the most intimate bonds.”

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "The production is instead so overpumped and overplayed as to be hardly comprehensible is the result of a fundamental misunderstanding of the musical, which is plenty complicated as written."

criticReviews.author: Gillian Russo
criticReviews.excerpt: "Short of lightning-fast rap battles, if anything can make a group of dead white men talking interesting, it's the knowledge that we're really watching a lively, fresh generation of actors making their names known and their voices heard."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "You leave the production newly amazed by the radical contingency of history as we know it...The spirit of ’76 still haunts America, for better and for worse."

criticReviews.author: James Frankie Thomas
criticReviews.excerpt: "I find myself deeply moved by the collective work to bring out the beauty and joy in such a fundamentally corrupted musical, and I’m glad to have witnessed it. I want other people to witness it."

criticReviews.author: Helen Shaw
criticReviews.excerpt: "Stern looks do not, politically and artistically, get us very far, but great musical moments still have power: they win the signatures; they rally the troops; they ring the bell."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "In truth, the conceit of the production doesn’t add any significant extrinsic meanings to the musical."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "At its best, the Roundabout’s production of '1776' ... shakes off any undue weight of expectation, treating the audience to classic musical theater songs sung by voices that have never before been given access."

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "This '1776' allows audience to witness a history anew through an outsider’s eye, as it reframes the classic Trumbull painting in a different light...one that inspires, yes, but one that also continues to haunt in its incompleteness."

criticReviews.author: Elisabeth Vincentelli
criticReviews.excerpt: "It all looks and sounds great, but the clock is ticking — therapy! — and we are no closer to understanding the real Neil."

criticReviews.author: Frank Scheck
criticReviews.excerpt: "The real reason for a show like this, of course, is not to do a deep dive into its subject’s psyche but rather to deliver full-throttle versions of the hits that baby boomers, those theatergoers with the most disposable income, grew up hearing."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "Despite being a lukewarm look at the Brooklyn-born superstar, the show headlined by Will Swenson will nonetheless appeal to Diamond’s ardent fans...Plenty of theatregoers at my performance didn’t have to be asked twice or need another sip of “Red, Red Wine” to noisily join in."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: " 'A Beautiful Noise' is a suitable tribute to him; in its biggest numbers it resembles an old-school Vegas-style impersonation show, recreating concert moments for the benefit of an audience that is happy to embark on a musical nostalgia trip."

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "The thing is, there’s just not much of a show there. The show and the audience aren’t here for the storm clouds, they’re here for the good times, which never seemed so good."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "This smoothly produced show’s presentation of his semi-symphonic rock and sentimental balladry failed to convert me. I’m still not a believer...'A Beautiful Noise' merely underscores the truth that, to tweak the cliché, beauty is in the ear of the listener."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "The musical’s decision to save it up till the end provides one of its more emotional moments...'A Beautiful Noise' could have used some dramatic stakes from the get-go."

criticReviews.author: New York Daily News
criticReviews.excerpt: "Diamond was a kind of talisman, and his music, filled with his signature blend of macho groan and sweet melodiousness, is complex enough to stand a show like this."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "It doesn’t break ground or dazzle with an unusual recipe, but it delivers reliable pleasures with polished professionalism and infectious energy...If there’s a secret ingredient that gives the musical version a zest, it is the wonderful score...Certainly not without its formulaic or sentimental aspects. Few mainstream musicals are. But it captures both the milieu it evokes and the colorful characters who populate it with a buoyancy and humor that ultimately won me over."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "There goes the neighborhood. Just when it was getting cool to go to a Broadway musical, along comes the lumbering and hackneyed 'A Bronx Tale'...A musically unmemorable mix of sappiness and contrived melodrama...Aside from Machiavelli-quoting mobster Bobby—played with expertly calibrated swagger by Nick Cordero—none of the characters command interest, and Alan Menken and Glenn Slater’s doo-wop–heavy score is far too lightweight for a plot that features murders."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "For all the craft and polish applied, this musical winds up right in the middle of the wrong place. It’s an unmoving target...Nothing rings true...The songs are all as professional and tuneful as you would expect from the team of Menken and Slater...They do perfectly well what songs are supposed to do in standard commercial musicals...But in doing so they normalize material that should not be normalized...That’s a shame; the musical is handsome and reasonably well performed."

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: "It takes everything that was good about 'A Bronx Tale' and waters it down until it’s as tasteless as a fast-food milkshake...Not only does Mr. Thornton’s relentlessly tautological first-person narration tell you what you just saw and are about to see, but so do Glenn Slater’s flat lyrics, which start out unpromisingly and get no better. Alan Menken’s music is Disneyfied doo-wop with some ersatz Sinatra thrown in, the stuff TV commercials are made of."

criticReviews.author: Jeremy Gerard
criticReviews.excerpt: "Generously plumped with ingredients from older, better shows, an easy-going familiarity suffuses 'A Bronx Tale,' along with the comforting glaze of nostalgia. They don’t make ’em like they yoozta (try as they might)...Astutely staged by Zaks and, OK, De Niro, 'A Bronx Tale' unfolds briskly...As to the score, like the story itself, it’s instantly forgettable. Every line and every rhyme comes roaring down the straightaway from a mile off."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "The show’s makers and shapers haven’t squandered their gifts. But they haven’t dug especially deep in the imagination department, either. 'A Bronx Tale' packs some tasty ear candy and fine performances, but it’s as conventional as it gets and could use a surprise or two...While the story unfolds strictly by the numbers, songs by Glenn Slater and Alan Menken lend periodic lifts. Menken is an ace at crafting Zelig-like melodies that evoke a period. Doo-wop and ‘60s pop loom large."

criticReviews.author: Marilyn Stasio
criticReviews.excerpt: "Credit director Jerry Zaks (and co-director Robert De Niro) with terrific casting...Let’s face it, this ill-advised musical version, with an anemic score by Alan Menken and Glenn Slater, isn’t going to send ’em dancing up the aisles. While there are fun things to be found, like those jailbait Doo-Wop Guys singing and snapping a cappella under the streetlight, the music is soggier than overcooked meatballs and the lyrics have absolutely no bite...Sergio Trujillo’s choreography is a snooze."

criticReviews.author: Frank Scheck
criticReviews.excerpt: "Because it resembles an urban fairy tale, Palminteri’s story works even better as a musical than it has in its earlier incarnations where its stereotypical aspects felt more glaring...'A Bronx Tale'—in the second half, packed with a succession of melodramatic incidents—can feel rushed and unconvincing...While the score doesn’t feature any breakout songs, it is tuneful and fun...Though hardly sophisticated entertainment, 'A Bronx Tale' has genuine charms."

criticReviews.author: Marianka Swain
criticReviews.excerpt: "you'll fall head over heels in love with this singular sensation of a dance musical"

criticReviews.author: Nick Curtis
criticReviews.excerpt: "a glorious parade of scintillating songs and snappy dance numbers"

criticReviews.author: Tim Bano
criticReviews.excerpt: "It’s a spectacular production of a musical that really doesn’t want to be spectacular."

criticReviews.author: David Benedict
criticReviews.excerpt: "The joy comes via punchy performances."

criticReviews.author: Helen Hawkins
criticReviews.excerpt: "high-kicking fun that's low on pathos"

criticReviews.author: Tim Robey
criticReviews.excerpt: "pure jazz-hands joy serves a dazzling celebration of the ensemble"

criticReviews.author: Alexis Soloski
criticReviews.excerpt: "This 'Carol,' is a lonelier affair. The script hews closely to the version that Dickens himself toured, with passages of prose narration that cut the goose-fat sentimentality with keen wit and gimlet detail."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "Another holiday season, another take on 'A Christmas Carol.' Like other theatrical versions of the classic, this one ends with the same words credited to Tiny Tim...a production this taut and well-told is its own sort of blessing."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "This splendid production is a Christmas miracle: The most theatrically fulfilling account of 'A Christmas Carol' that I have ever seen."

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "This is a grimmer take on Dickens’s story, full of fog and shadows."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "The staging is almost absurdly—and perhaps unnecessarily—lavish, although children and adults now accustomed to television series and movies that pour on the atmospherics with a ladle must, I suppose, be catered to."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "The true miracle of this production is that it, or rather, he (as in Mays) has us believing we’re encountering an entirely new work, with all the familiar beats and words and Dickensian lessons but layered with an honesty that makes the parts we’ve always told were scary genuinely scary."

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: "A cautionary tale for families with young kids: Christmas Eve nightmares may be caused...Nothing wrong with a good shudder at the holidays. Gets you in practice for the new year."

criticReviews.author: Marilyn Stasio
criticReviews.excerpt: "For all its dizzying charms, the overstuffed show doesn’t quite deliver on what really counts — the three Spirits of Christmas Past, Christmas Present and Christmas Future."

criticReviews.author: Marilyn Stasio
criticReviews.excerpt: "For all its dizzying charms, the overstuffed show doesn’t quite deliver on what really counts — the three Spirits of Christmas Past, Christmas Present and Christmas Future."

criticReviews.author: Linda Winer
criticReviews.excerpt: "Great Edward Albee, tepid production...although the play still dazzles with wit, gorgeous writing and the lurking terror of mortality, Director Pam MacKinnon spells things out here instead of letting Albee toy with us through suggestion and suspense. Nothing, alas, is delicate."

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt: "As you would expect of these highly accomplished, multi-award-winning cast members, none of them are bad. But they’re giving us the play, instead of living it."

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: "Pam MacKinnon directs this solid revival with a keen ear for the curling, teasing rhythms of Albee’s ornate lines, and the performances are top-notch...this Pulitzer winner still stings and sings."

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: Things finally become interesting, even zany, in the second scene of the second act. Until then, though, “A Delicate Balance” comes across like a dramatically static rewrite of “Virginia Woolf” with rather less drinking and much less cursing."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "Whip-smart and wickedly funny, the 1966 play is showcased in a very good production that’s cool, well-composed and captivating."

criticReviews.author: Marilyn Stasio
criticReviews.excerpt: "A Delicate Balance is no play for sissies...a brilliantly constructed if ultimately unfathomable play that only Edward Albee can get away with writing."

criticReviews.author: David Rooney
criticReviews.excerpt: "Whether audiences are encountering A Delicate Balance for the first time or for reappraisal, watching the six supremely accomplished actors  in this cast bite into their roles is thrilling."

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: "Albee's gift to humanity, you might say: a pleasurable three acts of watching others teeter on the brink, which always helps you last another day on terra firma yourself."

criticReviews.author: Linda Winer
criticReviews.excerpt: "Great Edward Albee, tepid production...although the play still dazzles with wit, gorgeous writing and the lurking terror of mortality, Director Pam MacKinnon spells things out here instead of letting Albee toy with us through suggestion and suspense.
