It will leave you unsettled and questioning the motives of its characters like any suspenseful piece of work will do. And in my opinion, that is its strongest asset."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "In 'Peter Pan Goes Wrong,' which opened Wednesday at the Ethel Barrymore Theater...the jokes and mishaps are still funny, if not quite as magical the second time around."

criticReviews.author: Allison Considine
criticReviews.excerpt: "Children (and children at heart) willing to ride the giggle train will enjoy this production the most."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "The best way to enjoy 'Peter Pan Goes Wrong,' in fact, may be to take it as some kind of comedy of errors...the game resilience of the actors—as they suffer through relentless variations on disaster slapstick—gets a little tiring, at least for me, when offered in a two-hour dose."

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "The bread and butter of Peter Pan’s humor is broad and full of grievous injuries. Like most carb-and-fat combinations, that means it goes down easy but risks leaving us too sated too soon."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: " PPGW uses a play-within-a-play structure as both loving tribute to theater and knowing satire on the narcissism and fearlessness required to make it."

criticReviews.author: New York Daily News
criticReviews.excerpt: “...'Peter Pan Goes Wrong' will be a great night out for a family audience. The politically incorrect show is a total blast and one of the very few Broadway attractions where kids are encouraged to clap, boo and talk back to the annoying actors."

criticReviews.author: A.D. Amorosi
criticReviews.excerpt: “ 'Peter Pan Goes Wrong' goes long and belabors its physical and vocal antics. But in general, too much of a good thing is a great thing here."

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: " 'Peter Pan Goes Wrong' exceedingly well. I mean to say, it goes right by going very wrong and avoiding ever going right."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: “At just 1 hour and 45 minutes, with no intermission, a play should not feel padded, but it does. Still, it is hardly without its pleasures: It’s funnier than expected, and Sher’s poetic naturalism as he creates stage pictures is always moving to watch. “

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: “As in any play about a family, White covers expected territory about generational divides, legacies, mortality, and finally, love.”

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: “White’s ‘Pictures From Home’ sometimes feels like an illustrated lecture about itself, and of images that are meant to say enough on their own.”

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: “ ‘Pictures From Home,’ the play, ends up being a very good argument for ‘Pictures From Home,’ the memoir, but not much of one for itself.”

criticReviews.author: Helen Shaw
criticReviews.excerpt: “Sultan’s portraiture was a combination of candid and staged, exquisitely composed in a way that Sher’s production is not...Everything onstage looks cold by contrast.”

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: “...’Pictures From Home’ remains two-dimensional. It’s more a comic gloss on the family’s sometimes fractious but loving relationships than the more searching examination of the images we project, in photos and in life, in contrast to the murkiness of our interior lives, that the play seems to be striving toward.”

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: “While the intimate and honest views of a family’s inner workings can’t help but touch our hearts at steadily paced moments, ‘Pictures From Home’ is too blunt in its characterizations...we can’t help but feeling sympathy for all concerned, characters and actors, but, sad to say, it’s the arguments we’ll remember.”

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: “As Broadway obsesses over youth and revolt, here’s a sweet and wise Broadway play about just wanting your mom and dad to keep on going, to wish they could live for ever and to realize that any artist can complain and roar but some wise ones choose instead to render their loved ones immortal.”

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "Though jolly enough, the latest Broadway incarnation... has a sweaty quality, bordering on frenzy, that’s hopelessly at odds with the cool wit of the original."

criticReviews.author: Austin Fimmano
criticReviews.excerpt: "Thoughtfully and lovingly updated for a modern audience, there’s something for everyone in this production."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Enjoy this Broadway hybrid that is tuneful and poetical: A most delightful model of a modern operettical."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "The exclamation mark really is the giveaway. In the making of Pirates! The Penzance Musical, an exquisitely funny, meticulously concocted theatrical pavlova"

criticReviews.author: Christian Lewis
criticReviews.excerpt: "Still, it is easy enough to put aside almost all quibbles about genre tensions or adaptation choices because the production is so joyous and well-executed."

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "a musical that’s otherwise effervescent, gorgeously sung, hysterical and frivolous"

criticReviews.author: Zachary Stewart
criticReviews.excerpt: "The finished product is operetta as political compromise, in which everyone gets a little taste of what they want, but never enough to be truly satisfied."

criticReviews.author: David Barbour
criticReviews.excerpt: "For Pierce's fans, it's probably unmissable, but a clearer vision would make a better, more coherent night out."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "Despite the wearying efforts of a likable cast headed by Matthew Broderick and Sarah Jessica Parker, the passage of 54 years is more than enough to reveal the triptych of one-act plays as uninhabitable in 2022...You could, I suppose, investigate 'Plaza Suite' as a catalog of male failings in midcentury America...In any case, that’s not what the current production is offering. Rather, it seems to hope we will look forgivingly enough on our benighted past to excuse it with a 'that’s how things were' shrug and laugh."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "4/5 stars...The show packs moments that are gleefully LOL, is deeper than you might expect, and the real-life married stars co-piloting this vintage vehicle are in fine form...In his Broadway debut as a director, Tony-winning actor John Benjamin Hickey displays a deft hand and sure instincts. He keeps the pacing brisk, while his smart tweak to the end of Act 2 is a playful and up-to-date improvement to the original script. Strong work by the cast...is matched by the production team."

criticReviews.author: Helen Shaw
criticReviews.excerpt: "In all three plays, Hickey and his actors have found many little moments for physical comedy...but these jolts are rarely enough to create a sustained energy. The same is true for the evening as a whole. I know you can’t wander around rewriting Simon, but maybe they could have just … skipped the middle one-act? That one’s a cold cocktail frankfurter, I’ll tell you that...In 'Plaza Suite,' I found that fragile funny-sad balance tipped too far toward melancholy, possibly because Broderick’s left-of-center delivery makes so much room for it."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "Although Mr. Broderick and Ms. Parker labor mightily to reanimate Simon’s 1968 comedy, their staunch but sometimes strained efforts, and the play’s undeniable fustiness—especially with regard to the relationships between men and women at its center—result in a production that tends to sag between the volleys of wisecracks that suffuse early Simon plays."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "Directed by John Benjamin Hickey with a clear reverence for Simon and the theatrical era in which his 1968 comedy titillated matinee audiences, this new 'Plaza Suite' feels mostly like an exercise in nostalgia – for a couple we’ve watched grow up, for a Broadway that demands little, and for the late playwright whose contributions to popular culture go far beyond this mid-level effort...John Lee Beatty has designed an absolutely gorgeous recreation of that hotel of dreams, and costume designer Jane Greenwood outfits the cast in lovely and, when necessary, witty, period attire."

criticReviews.author: Daniel D'Addario
criticReviews.excerpt: "The real-life married couple bring a serious commitment to the spirit of the work, allowing their own personas to throw some metatextual sparks without overtaking the spirit of Simon. As directed by John Benjamin Hickey, Parker and Broderick provoke, alienate and woo one another, and provide a strong argument for a playwright whose work seems next-to-impossible to subvert...The three pieces vary in tone, but throughout, the two stars share not merely an unmistakable chemistry but a shared willingness to dig into the work on its own terms. They almost entirely resist looking at 'Plaza Suite' through a 2022 lens."

criticReviews.author: David Rooney
criticReviews.excerpt: "Alas, the stars’ efforts, while certainly appealing, don’t make the material any less obsolete, a throwback to the bougie boulevard comedies that were once a Broadway staple. The observations on marriage and relationships occasionally generate a chuckle, but more often seem stale and the sexual politics retrograde, something that John Benjamin Hickey’s serviceable direction can’t disguise...Parker ultimately walks away with the show; she doesn’t lose the mannerisms that have become essential parts of her screen persona, but she molds them into three distinct characters, finding obvious enjoyment in reconnecting with her stage roots."

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: "Matthew Broderick is at peak Broderick. Theater people will understand this is not good news. It means that he’s delivering yet another bland, mousy smudge of a performance, squeaking his lines, looking like someone poured pudding in his loafers...Faced with this acting void, a.k.a. her husband, Parker gamely attempts pluck and passion as a series of unfulfilled wives and mothers...For both actors, 'Plaza Suite' ought to be a wonderful workout, a chance to show off versatility while nailing Simon’s well-crafted yuks. Instead, it feels like community theater for rich people."

criticReviews.author: David Wright
criticReviews.excerpt: "While the story has been through many iterations and abridgments—novel, play, Broadway musical, movie—the Met’s three-and-a-half-hour version presented nearly every note the composer wrote."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: “What is too much for the world is way too much for the play. And the play, for all its urgency, is already way too much. Running just over three hours, ‘Prayer for the French Republic,’...is still not long enough to do justice to the multiple histories it wants to tell.”

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: “It’s a plus-size play about big social issues that impresses in large structural ways as well as small moments...so this ‘Prayer’ will likely always be relevant. That’s a dramatic triumph – and a scorching reality.”

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: “There is perceptiveness and humor in ‘Prayer for the French Republic,’ and Cromer’s direction does its best to keep things honest. But as Harmon weighs out the issues, you can sense his thumb on the scale; by the denouement, it feels more like his whole hand, pressing for amens.”

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: “Though it’s surrounded by heavy clouds, Harmon’s play is plenty sharp and by no means gloomy...How much you respond to ‘Prayer’ may ultimately rest on your taste for such harangues. I admit to finding them hard to follow — not intellectually but emotionally. They leave me cold and a little suspicious.”

criticReviews.author: Helen Shaw
criticReviews.excerpt: “Like any play transferring to Broadway from an Off Broadway success, this ‘Prayer’ is a counterproposal to its earlier, smaller, and more intimate iteration.”

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: “ 'Prayer for the French Republic' addresses, with nuance, detail and understated passion, the tensions and the connections between history and current events."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: “...Edwards and his castmates bring two distinct, if not always so dissimilar, eras to life, and they tell a sweeping story while conveying genuine intimacy. ‘Prayer for the French Republic’ asks big questions – of history, of family, of identity – and, all but miraculously, answers their call.”

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: “The play, narrated uneasily by the self-doubting Patrick, is saying that little has been solved, the Jew remains a wanderer by necessity, that the painful lessons of history have never been more important, and love and happiness must be grabbed where it can.”

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt: “An uneven but enjoyable production…Let us give thanks for what Mr. Kline, embodying the capricious god of his own theatrical universe, has wrought. It is hard not to wish that the heavy farcical high jinks that surround him were on his high level…The staging by Mr. von Stuelpnagel brings out the more boisterous aspects of Coward’s comedy, occasionally to hilarious, but just as often labored, ends. And the pace needs to be picked up throughout.”

criticReviews.author: Marc Miller
criticReviews.excerpt: “Overplaying is a quality director Moritz von Stuelpnagel has unfortunately encouraged in most of the supporting cast. But Essendine himself can’t be overplayed, and Kline has a high old time accenting every aspect of the character’s showy personality…‘Present Laughter’ hasn’t aged quite as gracefully as its hero. It’s wonderfully literate, of course…But it’s 20 minutes longer than it has to be, it ends on a false happy-ending note, and its portrait of celebrity is very much of its time."

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: “An absolutely splendid revival…The simple act of handing America’s greatest exemplar of comic suavity a role he was born to play is half the battle…Kline is the very model of a star who lets his brilliance illuminate everyone around him…He enlivens each moment with palpable zest and impeccable style, arrogant brio shading into middle-aged insecurity with a twitch of his perfectly trimmed mustache. He must do more Coward or share his secrets.”

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: “The production takes seriously the mess that radiates from Garry’s narcissism, and with that seriousness refuels the hilarity of the farce that overlays it. In the hands of Kline and a vividly intelligent supporting cast, it’s a great and frank and still modern comedy…The play’s three-act structure is pretty much faultless…If there are still some extravagances to prune and shaggy moments to comb out, they’re minor.”

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: "Not only is Mr. Kline’s performance a triumph, but this revival is the best staging of a Coward play—any Coward play—that I’ve ever seen...Essendine is played for truth, not as a caricature, which simultaneously makes him more interesting and even funnier...By having his actors underplay the first half of the show, Mr. von Stuelpnagel heightens the payoff of the second half...By evening’s end, the laughter is loud, continuous and entirely well-deserved."

criticReviews.author: Jeremy Gerard
criticReviews.excerpt: “Moritz von Stuelpnagel’s revival is fleet, funny, deliciously cast and over-the-top when it should be–and occasionally when it needn’t be, sweating just a bit too hard to earn the audience’s whoops of pleasure. Fortunately, Coward and Kline are too dynamic a duo to suffer any damage from such picked nits. Chief among the other pleasures are Kate Burton…Peter Francis James and Reg Rogers…Less chief among the pleasures are Kristine Nielsen...Bavesh Pavel.”

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: “When your main character is a human peacock, you need an actor who can preen like nobody's business. Paging Kevin Kline, a debonair clown, who's ideally cast as the aging, mirror-mad matinee idol…Deadpan delivery? Funny physical bits? Check. Check…At times you’d like to hush the talky play…Cobie Smulders is saucy and sexy. Kristine Nielsen is reliably hilarious…Under the smart direction of Moritz von Stuelpnagel the production is in fine feather.”

criticReviews.author: Marilyn Stasio
criticReviews.excerpt: “A delicious drawing-room comedy…Kline relishes the comic challenge in this snazzy production…Director von Stuelpnagel has assembled a cast of reliable pros who know the drill so well they could pace it out in their sleep. The lesser-skilled younger actors should study the technique of these veterans and bless their lucky stars for the opportunity to do so. Kristine Nielsen, who plays Garry’s secretary, Monica Reed, constitutes a master class.”

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt: “An uneven but enjoyable production…Let us give thanks for what Mr. Kline, embodying the capricious god of his own theatrical universe, has wrought. It is hard not to wish that the heavy farcical high jinks that surround him were on his high level…The staging by Mr. von Stuelpnagel brings out the more boisterous aspects of Coward’s comedy, occasionally to hilarious, but just as often labored, ends. And the pace needs to be picked up throughout.”

criticReviews.author: Marc Miller
criticReviews.excerpt: “Overplaying is a quality director Moritz von Stuelpnagel has unfortunately encouraged in most of the supporting cast. But Essendine himself can’t be overplayed, and Kline has a high old time accenting every aspect of the character’s showy personality…‘Present Laughter’ hasn’t aged quite as gracefully as its hero. It’s wonderfully literate, of course…But it’s 20 minutes longer than it has to be, it ends on a false happy-ending note, and its portrait of celebrity is very much of its time."

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: “An absolutely splendid revival…The simple act of handing America’s greatest exemplar of comic suavity a role he was born to play is half the battle…Kline is the very model of a star who lets his brilliance illuminate everyone around him…He enlivens each moment with palpable zest and impeccable style, arrogant brio shading into middle-aged insecurity with a twitch of his perfectly trimmed mustache. He must do more Coward or share his secrets.”

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: “The production takes seriously the mess that radiates from Garry’s narcissism, and with that seriousness refuels the hilarity of the farce that overlays it. In the hands of Kline and a vividly intelligent supporting cast, it’s a great and frank and still modern comedy…The play’s three-act structure is pretty much faultless…If there are still some extravagances to prune and shaggy moments to comb out, they’re minor.”

Kristine Nielsen, who plays Garry’s secretary, Monica Reed, constitutes a master class.”

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt: "Ms. Barks is clearly a talented singer and actress...she has been given no chance to banish stardust memories of the woman who created her part. Directed and choreographed as if on automatic pilot by Jerry Mitchell. Its creators have hewed suffocatingly close to the film’s story, gags, and dialogue...Mostly, Ms. Barks conducts herself like a peppy, tomboyish cutup from a sitcom. She often doesn’t seem entirely at ease, but her discomfort is nothing compared to Mr. Karl’s."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Mostly just a dutiful replica of the movie...Not only does this approach miss an opportunity to rethink the story’s sugar-daddy fantasy in a deeper way, it also gets stale fast; this ain’t our first time on Rodeo Drive...Adams and Vallance’s music does its job, but has a Broadway show ever had lyrics so utterly, almost senselessly generic?...The cast makes the most of what 'Pretty Woman' allows them."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "'Pretty Woman: The Musical' has plenty of problems outside of its politics...It’s the kind of lifeless clunker that makes your heart go out to its actors...It’s more concerned with checking the boxes of all the movie’s most famous moments than it is with telling us anything new about these characters or creating any sense of surprise...The musical has added only 30 minutes to the length of the movie, and it still manages to feel draggy and overpadded."

criticReviews.author: Michael Schulman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Reports that the creators...were 'reshaping' the story for the #MeToo era have been greatly exaggerated...But Lawton and the film’s director, the late Garry Marshall, who co-wrote the book, have clearly taken a 'don’t mess with success' approach...Samantha Barks is agreeable as Vivian, and Andy Karl is an appealingly handsome Edward. The bright spots, though, come from the supporting cast...But it’s clear that the all-male creative team hasn’t interrogated the story."

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: "Not that 'Pretty Woman' is terrible—it’s just mediocre, albeit to a mind-boggling degree...Not only are the 16 songs banal, but they’re untheatrical: Virtually all of them are here’s-how-I’m-feeling-right-this-second power ballads that stop the action of the show dead instead of pushing it forward to the final curtain...Rarely in the history of Broadway has a bigger, staler nothingburger been served up than 'Pretty Woman.'"

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "Bland MOR songs, costumes mistaking gaudy for glitzy, and a sugary lead performance add up to one very smudged, very ill-fitting glass slipper...Hits all the film’s beats, crams in a roster of generic-sounding songs written by raspy-voiced ’90s power balladeer Bryan Adams (along with Jim Vallance), and gins up unconvincing nods to empowerment without for a moment thinking them through or taking them seriously."

criticReviews.author: Bob Verini
criticReviews.excerpt: "Stubbornly inconsequential, it’s a morally uplifting fairy tale of which everyone, young and old alike, can be skeptical...Director-choreographer Jerry Mitchell and team toss a decided gloss over this G-rated version of Hollywood nights, with production numbers and ensemble acting executed with exaggerated musical-comedy snap...Though the lyrics teem with cliche, the cast gives its all to sell them."

criticReviews.author: David Rooney
criticReviews.excerpt: "While the creative team strains a tad too diligently to give the female lead agency and sidestep the Cinderella story's awkward sexual politics, the show is best appreciated as a retro pleasure, guilty or not...Its chief reason to exist is as a nostalgia exercise, not a fresh entertainment in its own right. The songs are almost superfluous...Barks makes a sensational Broadway debut...Vivian probably could have done without the blunt literalness of lyrics by Adams and Vallance."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: “One-person, multicharacter stories often fail to develop suspense and momentum, but Miller has structured this one precisely...The abandonment of that structure in the play’s final third is likewise precise, and many will value the disruption ‘prima facie’ — at first glance.”

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: “Miller, an Australian writer with a law background, makes ’Prima Facie’ a message play. What it’s saying isn’t revelatory, but it is worthwhile. And Comer is a first-class messenger.”

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: “Her [Comer] virtuosity is not just a game—it’s emotional. Miller builds a respectable case, but Comer argues it brilliantly.”

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: “If the writing and production falter, Comer’s performance speaks more than clearly than all that’s going on around her...Arguments may be convincing in the abstract. But it’s in staying with a singular case, making you feel for a wholly realized person, that Comer articulates what’s real, urgent, and unbearable.”

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: “This urgent drama about the legal and emotional brutalities women often endure when they file charges of rape, particularly against a friend, lover or even husband, strikes home with scalding power.”

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: “The drama is in how Tessa deals with the crumbling of her ideals and the smashing of her self-delusions, and in how Comer can so vividly, indelibly display both.”

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: “ ‘Prima Facie’ manages to be both political and commercially viable theater, a rare feat these days, and one achieved here through the quality of this gifted actor, the talent and craft of the writer and the rich layering of experiential tension in the direction.”

criticReviews.author: Trish Deitch
criticReviews.excerpt: “This show, starring a popular television actress, will do its part in chipping away at the injustice that is women remaining voiceless and powerless after they’ve been sexually assaulted. And for that, ‘Prima Facie’ deserves high praise—even adulation.”

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt: "Watching this production’s overtaxed ensemble perform vignettes from different musicals...is like hearing a rushed raconteur drop name after famous name, without bothering to explain their significance...They’re a likable group, and I don’t fault them for the impression I often had that I was at a dinner theater...I recalled how often in my years of theatergoing performances in Prince’s shows have evoked similar shivers. If only such reminders came more frequently in this motley production."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "There’s little insight into Prince’s craft or his vision...The songs wind up in an awkward space: divorced from the dramatic context that gave many of them their power, yet too tethered to their first incarnations to enjoy the interpretive mobility they might have in a straightforward concert...'Prince of Broadway' does provide a fine showcase for several of the artists...It’s a pleasant collection of beloved and familiar Broadway songs, but there isn’t much to it."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "Though the music soars, the show’s central figure remains a bit generic, a bit out of focus...The company truly comes alive when they are freed from the task of walking us through Prince’s polished-up biography and allowed to do what they do best: break into song. The beauty lies in this tour through an astonishing array of musical gems...'Prince' is attempting something unique and admirable. but...the revue form doesn’t actually lend itself to demonstrating directorial brilliance."

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: "Modest though it is, 'Prince of Broadway' looks and sounds fabulous...The weak link is David Thompson’s book, in which Mr. Prince’s cliché-prone first-person reminiscences are placed in the mouths of the actors, always to unilluminating, momentum-killing effect. For the most part, though, 'Prince' adds up to a pleasingly intimate musical revue full of shining moments, albeit one that feels rather more like a pledge-week TV special than a full-fledged Broadway show."

criticReviews.author: Jeremy Gerard
criticReviews.excerpt: "'Prince of Broadway' bristles with the joyful noise of familiar songs delivered by a gifted and versatile cast...But what’s the through-line connecting one Hal Prince show with another?...That’s why 'Prince of Broadway' is, despite the warm bath of the Broadway songbook, such a colossal disappointment...The show fails to make the case for one of the greatest showmen of our time."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "You couldn’t wish for a more ideal place than Broadway to honor Prince. But you could wish for a better, more illuminating show in which to do it...One can’t help but be impressed by the scope and breadth—but at the same time feel left in the dark about Prince’s precise contributions...It’s not a deep dive into the mind of a master—more like Shallow Hal. If you’re okay with that and want to luxuriate in moments from some wonderful shows, you’ll be entertained by the cast."

criticReviews.author: Marilyn Stasio
criticReviews.excerpt: "The best 16 shows on Broadway are all playing in 'Prince of Broadway,' a sumptuous revue...Watching the hits flash by, like diamonds on a necklace, is sure to make you cry–with tears of joy if you saw that particular show, and tears of regret if you missed it...The talent that went into this show is out of this world...Unbeatable as an ensemble, cast members also get their individual moments to soar...You may wish 'Prince of Broadway' were twice as long, but you won’t go away hungry."

criticReviews.author: David Rooney
criticReviews.excerpt: "Sample-size nuggets that touch on the magic while leaving you craving more...This recap of an illustrious career leaves no doubt about the validity of Prince's exalted status, even if it’s thin on illuminating detail...What buoys 'Prince' is the polished presentation and elaborate design elements. But even more so it's the depth of characterization achieved...There's generally enough vitality in the staging and performances to help overcome the shortage of personal insights."

criticReviews.author: Elisabeth Vincentelli
criticReviews.excerpt: " 'Punch' comes up short in capturing the exchange between the victim’s family and the perpetrator because it always leans on Jacob’s perspective"

criticReviews.author: Caroline Cao
criticReviews.excerpt: "It doesn’t stick the landing, but it leaves one last thought: Forgiveness isn’t a clear-cut route for everyone."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "While story itself is inspiring, some central emotional focus seems missing from the way it unfolds in Punch, which winds up feeling less like a full-blown play and more like a digressive PSA about the dangers of street fighting"

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "The tempo of Punch slows and the performances sharpen and deepen. Though the air is thick with anguish, three people start to grope their way through it toward each other."

criticReviews.author: Emlyn Travis
criticReviews.excerpt: "Will Harrison delivers an impactful performance in Broadway play inspired by real-life tragedy"

criticReviews.author: David Gordon
criticReviews.excerpt: " 'Punch' ends on an upbeat note, one that some may find saccharine. But the optimism signals that Jacob’s hard work of transformation paid off. "

criticReviews.author: David Barbour
criticReviews.excerpt: "It dares to posit that forgiveness is the ultimate response to irreparable loss, an idea that may make it the most radical play in town."

criticReviews.author: Howard Miller
criticReviews.excerpt: "Any play that attempts to dramatize a non-fiction book-length account is bound to overemphasize some points and skim past others, and that is the case with 'Punch'."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: CRITIC’S PICK: “‘Purlie Victorious’...is every bit as scathingly funny as the 1961 reviews said it was. But even though times have surely changed everything dark in the play is still dark, and the lightness no less necessary.”

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "Flat-out hilarious and stacked with topflight performances led by Leslie Odom, Jr. and Kara Young, 'Purlie Victorious' is also a triumph when it comes to timing. Suffice it to say the play speaks directly to today’s racial tumult."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: “ ‘Purlie Victorious’ is uncompromising in its defiance, but it rarely feels preachy. Its medicine goes down with a heap of dark brown sugar.”

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: “In a lot of ways, ’Purlie’ is a trickster story, which means it runs on a combination of brains, guts, and charisma”

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: “ ‘Purlie Victorious’ was a radical play for Broadway in 1961, when the civil-rights movement was garnering national attention...The play remains radical today, and for the same reason...More important, the production, directed by Kenny Leon, Broadway’s go-to helmer of black-themed plays reinvigorates the jesting that animates the antic action.”

criticReviews.author: Aramide Tinubu
criticReviews.excerpt: “The themes of ‘Purlie Victorious’ — segregation, racial terror and the unjustness of sharecropping — are no laughing matter. Yet the brilliance of the performers in this first Broadway revival since its original run, and their ability to lean into the playfulness of Davis’ comedy, present the euphoric and revelatory experiences of being Black while commenting on the absolute absurdity of racism.”

criticReviews.author: Peter Marks
criticReviews.excerpt: “The production treats us to this sort of divinely worked-out moment in every scene. Sometimes, a cast in a well-made comedy can let us know they’re playing for keeps and, at the same time, for fun. This is the fine line that ‘Purlie Victorious’ walks so beautifully.”

criticReviews.author: Christian Holub
criticReviews.excerpt: “The pleasures of ’Purlie Victorious’ aren't just verbal. The high-energy production often has the physicality of a top-notch farce, with characters running back and forth across the stage...’Purlie Victorious’ manages to have fun without shying away from the historical reality of Black oppression.”

criticReviews.author: Kenji Fujishima
criticReviews.excerpt: “Beyond the opportunity it offers to discover, or rediscover, Davis’s still-fresh, still-impressive play itself, she is arguably the best reason to catch this excellent production.”

criticReviews.author: David Barbour
criticReviews.excerpt: “I went into Purlie Victorious wondering if it might not feel dated or off-topic in terms of today's politics; I left in awe of the script's vigor, its distinctive mix of hilarity and righteous anger, and its insistence that, when it comes to racial injustice, we're all in it together. After a couple of seasons of plays filled with despair and anguish, Davis' humor has a bracing effect; countering evil with ridicule, he diminishes it, robbing it of its power. It's a weapon more playwrights could stand to wield.”

criticReviews.author: Howard Miller
criticReviews.excerpt: “Even while playing around with exaggerated stereotyping to accentuate the satirical comedy, it is clear that Ossie Davis, writing in the midst of the American Civil Rights Movement, strove mightily to achieve a balance between the ludicrous and a powerful message of equality and the potential for a better world. Everyone involved in this production has been able to articulate this balance to a high degree, so that we leave the theater on a decidedly positive and hopeful note, even if the hard work to bring that hope to fruition never ends.”

criticReviews.author: Frank Scheck
criticReviews.excerpt: “Satire doesn’t always age particularly well. Fortunately, the new production of Ossie Davis’ 1961 play ’Purlie Victorious’ has sidestepped any issues about its being dated for two reasons, one good and one bad. The good is that director Kenny Leon has provided such a breakneck, well-staged rendition, superbly performed by its terrific ensemble, that the fun never lags. The bad is that the issues depicted in the play have lost little of their resonance even in these supposedly ‘post-racial’ times.”

criticReviews.author: Steven Suskin
criticReviews.excerpt: “Most critical to the success of the evening, perhaps, is the work of director Leon. He honors Davis’s every intention, both written and unwritten in the script. And, more than that, he appears to be channeling what the author would want the play to stand for after the intervening 60-odd years, and how the wise activist Davis would address what is happening in the country right now.”

criticReviews.author: Brittani Samuel
criticReviews.excerpt: “There is nothing funny about the way racism has been codified into American systems of law, education, capitalism, etc. But shows like ‘Purlie Victorious’ work because they satirize the ludicrousness of these injustices and mock the partisans that continue to espouse them. The show should sit at the top of “must-see” lists for anyone who enjoys big-laugh comedies that take a piercing look at serious topics.”

criticReviews.author: Ron Fassler (critic)
criticReviews.excerpt: “Under the assured guidance of director Kenny Leon, the entire cast steps lightly, and boldly, at the same time: a magical feat. The show is beautifully paced, exquisitely designed (Derek McLane), costumed (Emilio Sosa) and lit (Adam Honoré); what’s more, it pays honor to legendary actor/writer/activist Ossie Davis with love and respect.”

criticReviews.author: Margret Echeverria
criticReviews.excerpt: “It’s classic comedy – bait and switch, slave out-smarting his master, disguises, romantic intrigue, spies, sex and triumph over evil...The wisdom is that humanity triumphs through comedy delivered with love which builds community and heals the tremendous pain of oppression.”

criticReviews.author: Elyse Trevers
criticReviews.excerpt: "Although 'Purlie Victorious' is a revival, the play feels very current. The audience hears no new message but the same humorous dialogue Davis wrote 60 years ago seems appropriate today. So this humor has a wry quality to it. Doesn’t feel like we’ve made much progress."

criticReviews.author: Nicole Serratore
criticReviews.excerpt: “The success of the play on the page and in this production, directed by Kenny Leon, comes from striking the right tone. The seriousness of the underlying issues is always present alongside the comedic gloss.  We are laughing while seeing the darkness in all the humor.”

criticReviews.author: Jonathan Mandell
criticReviews.excerpt: Odom must toggle between sounding like a comic mountebank (“I ain’t never in all my life told a lie I didn’t mean to make come true, some day!”) and like an impassioned civil rights advocate (“We want our cut of the Constitution…”) As deft as the acting is, the audience also winds up toggling – between the (sometimes outdated) comedy of the plot and the (often still timely) underlying outrage.

criticReviews.author: Brian Scott Lipton
criticReviews.excerpt: “These days, we’ve all become used to shots in the arm whose side effects only come to the fore a day or two later. ‘Purlie Victorious’ is that kind of much-needed theatrical medicine.”

criticReviews.author: Samuel L. Leiter
criticReviews.excerpt: Purlie Victorious, running a swift and intermissionless 100 minutes, is theatre for everyone: truly funny, socially meaningful, historically educational, politically progressive, appealingly accessible, emotionally inspiring, and marvelously performed. One hopes it’s still remembered when Tony time comes around.

criticReviews.author: Robert Hofler
criticReviews.excerpt: “Despite all his sermonizing, Purlie never turns into a pedagogue, thanks to Davis, who has loaded the preacher’s speeches with great one-liners and epigrams — none of which will be repeated here. They need to be experience first-hand in the theater...‘Purlie Victorious’ is the funniest show now performing on Broadway”

criticReviews.author: Mason Pilevsky
criticReviews.excerpt: Purlie Victorious commits to the power of theatre to make people uncomfortable, and also the value and necessity of doing so. In today’s world of short attention spans, many of us are used to being able to stop watching when something pushes us too far, but in a theatre we don't have that luxury. I'm grateful for theatrical spaces that makes people sit with their discomfort, process it, ride it out, and keep going. In addition to laughter, the play evoked serious ideas to ponder and percolate.

criticReviews.author: David Sheward
criticReviews.excerpt: “For a brief second, we are reminded of true venomous nature of the Old South. But then, the jokes continue, Ol’Cap’n gets his just desserts and ’Purlie’—both the character and the play— emerges truly victorious.”

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "Deeply imagined and grave beneath its yucks, it unspools like a brilliant sitcom. Then, also like a sitcom, it jumps the shark."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "Purpose is a daring dramatic vivisection of the fictional Jasper family... Director Phylicia Rashad has assembled an A-plus cast... [it] buzzes with rich ideas about sons and fathers and the burdens of legacy, sexuality, and authenticity."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Purpose is a big swing, but that’s what it takes to get a big hit."

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "...much of the nearly mathematical pleasure of watching Purpose lies in watching a top-tier craftsman set up and then launch one long domino chain of familial discord."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "“Purpose” doesn’t sustain the same level of excitement in its longer second act"

criticReviews.author: Aramide Tinubu
criticReviews.excerpt: "A whirlwind of a play, the cast delivers incredible performances"

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: ""It’s one of several that the playwright Branden Jacobs-Jenkins deploys to gasps and guffaws...a densely packed and blistering powder keg of a play about (among other things) legacy, faith, corruption and the limits of desire.""

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "I howled all the way through Jacobs-Jenkins’ clever and venomous spin on the story"

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "The Queen of Versailles swerves and overcorrects like a drunk driver. Tonally, it’s all over the map...It is the confused, contorted product of a set of absolutely incompatible impulses"

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "Rather than eat the rich, the musical settles for nipping them on the nose with all the ferocity of Jackie’s cuddly white Pomeranian."

criticReviews.author: David Barbour
criticReviews.excerpt: A big, splashy effort, slickly professional in nearly every aspect, that has no idea what to make of its heroine. It's a star vehicle with a giant question mark at its center, and its nonjudgmental gaze ultimately leaves one feeling surprisingly neutral.

criticReviews.author: Joseph Pisano
criticReviews.excerpt: It's neither a credible hero's journey nor a compelling antihero's one; it's simply soulless.

criticReviews.author: David Roberts
criticReviews.excerpt: “In a year when Broadway has given us genuinely ambitious work grappling with what it means to be American, "The Queen of Versailles" offers only spectacle without insight, a palace with no one home. What were they thinking?”

criticReviews.author: Mason Pilevsky
criticReviews.excerpt: The frivolous first act and the stirring second act deliciously dance together.

criticReviews.author: Cary Wong
criticReviews.excerpt: Chenoweth is, of course, the draw, and she tries her hardest to make the material work.

criticReviews.author: Laura Collins-Hughes
criticReviews.excerpt: Critic’s Pick: "more than an entertaining biomusical with a hummable score. Directed by Michael Arden, it’s also a sociological fairy tale"

criticReviews.author: Anna Paone
criticReviews.excerpt: "Duran and Raybould have pulled off something that is, if not impossible, extremely difficult: a comedic look at race that will have broad audience appeal. This fascinating show should have life beyond its current downtown run."

criticReviews.author: Laura Collins-Hughes
criticReviews.excerpt: "The considerable beauty of this inspiriting show — full of complicated emotions about our diaspora nation — is streaked with melancholy."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "The simplicity of the production provides breathing room in a megamusical that often exhilarates, but also drains because of its tendency to always think bigger."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "What he delivers in Ragtime is, quite simply, some of the most magnificent singing I have ever heard on Broadway"

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "The production is so powerfully sung and deeply felt that it overwhelms. Maybe these characters have false dreams, and maybe the show’s idea of hope is impossibly naïve, but it lingers."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "This sterling production, with its flawless cast and admirable trenchancy amid an extraordinarily complex plot, augurs well for her tenure."

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: “ 'Ragtime' is generous to all of its characters...But there is still something touching about its conviction that they will have a better life. I mean, Americans look to musicals for hope, don’t we?"

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "In productions large or small — or, here, imperfectly in-between, though still glorious — everything is the service of the show that creates with words, music and movement a grand American tapestry — tears and all."

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "Fortunately, the show sounds gloriously lush throughout...So much so that it hardly needs much embellishment at all."

criticReviews.author: Laura Collins-Hughes
criticReviews.excerpt: "The considerable beauty of this inspiriting show — full of complicated emotions about our diaspora nation — is streaked with melancholy."

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "Fortunately, the show sounds gloriously lush throughout...So much so that it hardly needs much embellishment at all."

criticReviews.author: Laura Collins-Hughes
criticReviews.excerpt: "it is a bouncy, crowd-pleasing comedy about female empowerment, self-acceptance and chasing one’s ambitions."

criticReviews.author: Kyle Turner
criticReviews.excerpt: "...it’s curious that, particularly in today's political environment, the show loops back to a relatively unquestioned idea about the meaning, value, and reality of the American dream."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "This show is a bona fide crowd pleaser: a warm hug that pulls you into its generous bosom. With a little luck, it could turn out to be a sleeper hit."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "funny, tender, compassionate and so well-performed by the eight women on stage that it earned a mid-show standing ovation the night I was in attendance."

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "It’s a joyous scene of empowerment, with the women taking prideful ownership of their bodies, their lives and the stage."

criticReviews.author: Meg Masseron
criticReviews.excerpt: "Real Women Have Curves offers far more than just its body-positive title. It may not be the flashiest musical of the season, but it’s real."

criticReviews.author: Kimberly Ramirez
criticReviews.excerpt: "The show pulses with a distinctly chingona spirit–it is bold and defiantly optimistic despite relentlessly biased"

criticReviews.author: Victor Gluck
criticReviews.excerpt: Not only a joyous entertainment, it is also a moving tribute to the immigrant experience.

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "the tree...onstage is among the most beautiful and wondrous theatrical creations"

criticReviews.author: Gillian Russo
criticReviews.excerpt: "Redwood...like the redwood tree, as we learn, its roots remain shallow."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "The show is all bark and no bite. "

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "for all its soaring vocals and vertical movement, Redwood leaves us stubbornly grounded."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "They wrap the show in visually alluring wallpaper. "

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "...you could call “Redwood” a musical chamber piece with monumentality"

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: "You want to leave shivering with the majesty of nature"

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "...the moral of the story make you want to go outside and touch grass"

criticReviews.author: Zachary Stewart
criticReviews.excerpt: "It is a delightful reminder that something that might at first appear uninteresting (a theatrical exploration of a mother-son relationship, sand) often conceals much mystery."

criticReviews.author: Loren Noveck
criticReviews.excerpt: "Rheology would not exist without that relationship and yet it transmutes those truths into something intensely theatrical"

criticReviews.author: Jonathan Mandell
criticReviews.excerpt: a sometimes brain-stretching exercise in physics and family.

criticReviews.author: Matt Wolf
criticReviews.excerpt: “The meat of the play is the intersection – and sometimes the sharp bifurcation – between the personal and the political at a time and place in history when one’s very choice of music can itself seem seditious...But, equally, ‘Rock ‘N’ Roll’ invites you to succumb to the innate musicality of the material, which exerts its own grip well before the company is seen rocking out collectively to the Rolling Stones.”

criticReviews.author: Franco Milazzo
criticReviews.excerpt: “Under Nina Raine's fluent direction, Parker is a solid presence throughout as the ever-tetchy Morrow... While Stoppard struggles here to give his female characters the same love and attention he pours into Max and Jan, Nancy Carroll is a real treat in the dual role of Eleanor and the adult Esme while Phoebe Horn adds bounce and energy throughout."

criticReviews.author: Arifa Akbar
criticReviews.excerpt: “Stoppard’s 2006 play asks important ideological questions with typically fizzing wordplay but its growling, feral energy comes too late”

criticReviews.author: Dave Fargnoli
criticReviews.excerpt: “Part trenchant political-history lecture, part slow-burning romantic comedy, Tom Stoppard’s 2006 drama is a sprawling, self-indulgent piece packed with fascinating ideas.”

criticReviews.author: Tim Bano
criticReviews.excerpt: “What makes it all worth it is the enduring quality of some of the writing. There are moments where Stoppard settles in and lets rip: big battling speeches about politics and humanity and all that good stuff. Zinging lines. Even emotion, bucking the received wisdom about Stoppard’s plays that head always beats heart.”

criticReviews.author: Aleks Sierz
criticReviews.excerpt: “Nathaniel Parker holds the play together with his mixture of opinionated anger and occasional moments of softer emotion...Still, the play still fascinates: come on oldies, let’s rock again!”

criticReviews.author: Claire Allfree
criticReviews.excerpt: “Stoppard clashes together multiple ideas in this lusty, messy, exuberant play, allowing almost every character to hang themselves on the ropes of their moral confusion while largely withholding judgement...’Rock n Roll’ contains, too, an eerily prescient note, the intimation that tanks and totalitarianism come in many forms. ”

criticReviews.author: Tom Wicker
criticReviews.excerpt: “This isn’t a biographical play. As the ideological conversations build and break over the years it spans, and cast members swap out one character for another, it’s really the story of a relationship – the fragile, often fraught one we have with our own beliefs.”

criticReviews.author: Sam Waite
criticReviews.excerpt: "The work of a famously skilled writer, 'Rock ‘N’ Roll' suffers at times from its own sprawling storyline, and the sheer amount it wants to say at any given time. This attractively staged revival serves as a reminder of the play’s strengths as both a political work and an exploration of a complex history, but also of its faults – too broad a scope, too twee and tidy an ending."

criticReviews.author: Rachel Halliburton
criticReviews.excerpt: “This is an evening as dazzling as it’s profound, a reminder that when Stoppard is on form he’s unbeatable.”

criticReviews.author: Erifyli Gigante
criticReviews.excerpt: “By focusing on the human aspect of political situations, ‘Rock ‘n’ Roll’ offers a nuanced exploration of hope and despair, leaving us with a mix of emotions about the future.”

criticReviews.author: Frey Kwa Hawking
criticReviews.excerpt: “Though this ‘Rock ‘n’ Roll’ sits fairly well at the Hampstead, perhaps a different take on the play could’ve given it a vibrancy lacking here.”

criticReviews.author: Alastair Ball
criticReviews.excerpt: "Performance, staging and music bring to life Stoppard’s brilliant writing and allow us to see intimately into these characters’ lives. The brilliance of 'Rock ‘n’ Roll' is that we are brought inside these personal moments where huge abstract political issues become character drama."

criticReviews.author: Hayley Levitt
criticReviews.excerpt: "'Rodgers and Hammerstein's Cinderella' Is a Lovely Night at Paper Mill Playhouse: The 2013 Broadway musical version of Cinderella comes to New Jersey for the holidays, starring Ashley Blanchet."

criticReviews.author: Marina Kennedy
criticReviews.excerpt: "'RODGERS + HAMMERSTEIN'S CINDERELLA' at Paper Mill Playhouse-An Elegant Treasure to Behold and Enjoy"

criticReviews.author: Bob Rendell
criticReviews.excerpt: "Miraculously, this is the 'Rodgers & Hammerstein Cinderella' the American musical theatre has been waiting for. It is as much a sophisticated, brilliantly witty, adult musical as it is an unfussy, down to earth, magical fairy tale for families."

criticReviews.author: Simon Saltzman
criticReviews.excerpt: “Rodgers and Hammerstein’s Cinderella”

criticReviews.author: Allen Neuner
criticReviews.excerpt: "'Rodgers + Hammerstein’s Cinderella' is a classic fairy tale with a clever modern sensibility"

criticReviews.author: Philip Dorian
criticReviews.excerpt: "Paper Mill Playhouse is giving a ball! 'Rodgers and Hammerstein’s Cinderella' in NJ"

criticReviews.author: Karen Nowosad
criticReviews.excerpt: "‘Cinderella’ is Filled with Music and Magic"

criticReviews.author: Beth Abramson Brier
criticReviews.excerpt: "This Updated Version is Purely Magical and Simply Charming"

criticReviews.author: Ruth Ross
criticReviews.excerpt: "UPDATED 'CINDERELLA' MAY LACK SOME MAGIC BUT PLEASES AS HOLIDAY FARE"
"'Cinderella' Shimmers at Paper Mill Playhouse"

criticReviews.author: Nick Curtis
criticReviews.excerpt: “This isn’t perfect, but it’s quite a ride.”

criticReviews.author: Arifa Akbar
criticReviews.excerpt: "It’s all rather hard to digest in around 100 minutes. There are more than a headful of ideas, while the personal stories are too brief to pull at your emotions."

criticReviews.author: Dave Fargnoli
criticReviews.excerpt: "Challenging, thought-provoking and sometimes gasp-inducingly close to the bone, this relentlessly twisty slice of speculative fiction"

criticReviews.author: Daz Gale
criticReviews.excerpt: “R.O.I. (Return On Investment) is a thrilling and unpredictable ride from start to finish.”

criticReviews.author: Gary Naylor
criticReviews.excerpt: "...a heady, head-spinning 90 minutes that starts in the dystopian near-past, Covid Times natch, and finishes in a dystopian near-future - and it’s all terrifyingly plausibly."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: “The play is thus less terrifying than teenifying — hence the plus sign instead of the ‘and’ in the title.”

criticReviews.author: Gillian Russo
criticReviews.excerpt: "By having a uniformly young cast, Romeo + Juliet successfully drives home the juvenile pettiness of the Montague/Capulet feud and sorrow...But this production of the love story hasn't quite found its heartbeat."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "What makes 'We Are Young' feel so right is more literal than all that: This Romeo and Juliet is very much about being young."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "...Sam Gold’s frenzied, youthful staging of the Shakespeare tragedy."

criticReviews.author: Trish Deitch
criticReviews.excerpt: "And the production is fun: The actors use the in-the-round theater to its fullest"

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: "...director Sam Gold's hyperpop reimagining of 'Romeo + Juliet.'"

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "The enthusiasm is thrilling, even when it almost flattens you underfoot."

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "During the dark final moments in the crypt...the play peters out."

criticReviews.author: Emlyn Travis
criticReviews.excerpt: "Kit Connor and Rachel Zegler are (violent) delights in Gen Z take on Shakespeare play"

criticReviews.author: Pete Hempstead
criticReviews.excerpt: "...this production is more for the kids"

criticReviews.author: David Barbour
criticReviews.excerpt: “I'm afraid this Romeo and Juliet is a largely one-sided affair.”

criticReviews.author: Howard Miller
criticReviews.excerpt: "...most-relatable entry level Shakespeare play to share with teenage students."

criticReviews.author: Victor Gluck
criticReviews.excerpt: "Sam Gold's youth-oriented reworking will please Gen Z more than their parents"

criticReviews.author: David Roberts
criticReviews.excerpt: "Their gender fluidity...embody the same characteristics in the tragedy itself."

criticReviews.author: Jonathan Mandell
criticReviews.excerpt: aimed unapologetically at Gen Z… sometimes the production thrilled…there are downsides

criticReviews.author: Samuel L. Leiter
criticReviews.excerpt: It’s hard to escape the feeling that the audience, regardless of age, is being patronized.

criticReviews.author: Thom Geier
criticReviews.excerpt: "Kit Connor is a magnetic Romeo, projecting all the eagerness...of a charismatic young"

criticReviews.author: Deirdre Donovan
criticReviews.excerpt: Sam Gold’s revival is bound to appeal to Generation Z.

criticReviews.author: Mason Pilevsky
criticReviews.excerpt: The love story marries theatre history with our present forms of entertainment.

criticReviews.author: Cary Wong
criticReviews.excerpt: A big welcome to what I’m dubbing Romeo + Juliet: The Jellicle Ball to Broadway.

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "Although it’s a relief to experience a phlegmatic instead of a violent Joan, it’s also a perplexity because the choice robs her of psychology. A hero and genius she may be, but somehow also inert...Still, when the play reaches its tragic sixth scene all that withholding pays off...If the production as a whole made up for the diminished dramatics with ample attention to its intellectual grandeur, it might even have seemed bracingly modern. Instead it just seems modest."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Shaw’s urbane determination to give every man his say shifts the play’s focus from its central girl for long stretches of prolix philosophical and legal badinage; Daniel Sullivan’s baggy, plainly designed revival is nearly three hours long and feels it, right up to Shaw’s quirky and deflating coda. Despite a capable cast...'Saint Joan' doesn’t rise to meet the contemporary energy of youthful protest with which it coincides. It flickers with intelligence but doesn’t burn."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "A sentimental, flattening approach that renders Joan dead in the water before she ever reaches the fire...in Sullivan’s positively inert revival...Shaw’s a tricky playwright—cantankerous and proudly verbose—but he’s also a ferocious wit...But if your first experience of Shaw or his Joan is Sullivan’s tepid production and its disappointingly soft starring turn by Rashad, you could be forgiven for writing this vigorous play and its fascinating playwright off as a collective bore."

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: "Condola Rashad is one of the most charismatic actors on the New York stage, but...she is by no means a classical actor. Her voice is neither resonant enough nor sufficiently varied in tonal color to allow her to speak Shaw’s etched dialogue compellingly...While I wish that Mr. Sullivan’s baldly straightforward production were more theatrically daring, the play comes through with bright clarity and makes, as always, a thought-provoking impression."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "Directed by Daniel Sullivan with an easy flow that appears to modernize the 1923 play and keep all that Shavian verbiage moving at a smart clip...Rashad’s Joan seems to have the peace of confidence. Still, I wouldn’t have minded a bit more fury before the fire...All is forgiven onstage (and for the most part, off) by the long play’s final scene, when Shaw reassembles even his dead characters 25 years after Joan’s burning, in a playful, ghosty, dreamy encounter of reconciliation."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "Holy misfire. Broadway’s 'Saint Joan' is a head-scratcher...The revival has as much crackle as soggy kindling...Rashad has a glint in her eye that grabs. But her star turn lacks mystery, might and command to hold you in her grip. Moreover, director Daniel Sullivan’s stubbornly unengaging staging curiously tilts toward comedy — actually, musical comedy."

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "Smart, stylish, and engaging...Rashad steps into the starring role in a blaze of glory and claims it as her own...Shaw never goes for the didactic slam-dunk, even when the angels are on his side. Instead he revels in the complexity of issues, motives and agendas in a dialectic that’s weighty even as it crackles with wit...In a handsome production, Sullivan deftly directs his first-class, deep-bench cast with subtle shadings of doubt and wonder."

criticReviews.author: Frank Scheck
criticReviews.excerpt: "Even when done well, 'Saint Joan' is a slog. And since MTC's revival isn't done very well, it's even more of a slog than usual...Rashad certainly possesses the necessary physical presence...But she never quite gets a handle on the role...Shaw's play is more academic than dramatic, largely consisting of indigestibly windy philosophical debates and monologues...In this visually monotonous, static production, you come away feeling that the dialogue would be much better read than heard."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "Although it’s a relief to experience a phlegmatic instead of a violent Joan, it’s also a perplexity because the choice robs her of psychology. A hero and genius she may be, but somehow also inert...Still, when the play reaches its tragic sixth scene all that withholding pays off...If the production as a whole made up for the diminished dramatics with ample attention to its intellectual grandeur, it might even have seemed bracingly modern. Instead it just seems modest."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Shaw’s urbane determination to give every man his say shifts the play’s focus from its central girl for long stretches of prolix philosophical and legal badinage; Daniel Sullivan’s baggy, plainly designed revival is nearly three hours long and feels it, right up to Shaw’s quirky and deflating coda. Despite a capable cast...'Saint Joan' doesn’t rise to meet the contemporary energy of youthful protest with which it coincides. It flickers with intelligence but doesn’t burn."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "A sentimental, flattening approach that renders Joan dead in the water before she ever reaches the fire...in Sullivan’s positively inert revival...Shaw’s a tricky playwright—cantankerous and proudly verbose—but he’s also a ferocious wit...But if your first experience of Shaw or his Joan is Sullivan’s tepid production and its disappointingly soft starring turn by Rashad, you could be forgiven for writing this vigorous play and its fascinating playwright off as a collective bore."

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: "Condola Rashad is one of the most charismatic actors on the New York stage, but...she is by no means a classical actor. Her voice is neither resonant enough nor sufficiently varied in tonal color to allow her to speak Shaw’s etched dialogue compellingly...While I wish that Mr. Sullivan’s baldly straightforward production were more theatrically daring, the play comes through with bright clarity and makes, as always, a thought-provoking impression."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "Directed by Daniel Sullivan with an easy flow that appears to modernize the 1923 play and keep all that Shavian verbiage moving at a smart clip...Rashad’s Joan seems to have the peace of confidence. Still, I wouldn’t have minded a bit more fury before the fire...All is forgiven onstage (and for the most part, off) by the long play’s final scene, when Shaw reassembles even his dead characters 25 years after Joan’s burning, in a playful, ghosty, dreamy encounter of reconciliation."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "Holy misfire. Broadway’s 'Saint Joan' is a head-scratcher...The revival has as much crackle as soggy kindling...Rashad has a glint in her eye that grabs. But her star turn lacks mystery, might and command to hold you in her grip. Moreover, director Daniel Sullivan’s stubbornly unengaging staging curiously tilts toward comedy — actually, musical comedy."

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "Smart, stylish, and engaging...Rashad steps into the starring role in a blaze of glory and claims it as her own...Shaw never goes for the didactic slam-dunk, even when the angels are on his side. Instead he revels in the complexity of issues, motives and agendas in a dialectic that’s weighty even as it crackles with wit...In a handsome production, Sullivan deftly directs his first-class, deep-bench cast with subtle shadings of doubt and wonder."

criticReviews.author: Frank Scheck
criticReviews.excerpt: "Even when done well, 'Saint Joan' is a slog. And since MTC's revival isn't done very well, it's even more of a slog than usual...Rashad certainly possesses the necessary physical presence...But she never quite gets a handle on the role...Shaw's play is more academic than dramatic, largely consisting of indigestibly windy philosophical debates and monologues...In this visually monotonous, static production, you come away feeling that the dialogue would be much better read than heard."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "Although it’s a relief to experience a phlegmatic instead of a violent Joan, it’s also a perplexity because the choice robs her of psychology. A hero and genius she may be, but somehow also inert...Still, when the play reaches its tragic sixth scene all that withholding pays off...If the production as a whole made up for the diminished dramatics with ample attention to its intellectual grandeur, it might even have seemed bracingly modern. Instead it just seems modest."
